title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
summary: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

AI.tldr: 模仿策略在执行中会累积小误差导致失败；作者用离线学习的动作仿射世界模型预测"小修正"的局部响应，在线只需一次模型评估加一次凸二次规划求解即可精修动作。四个仿真操作任务上成功率在对比基线中最高，单控制步平均精修开销 3.8 ms（不含基础策略采样）。
AI.motivation: 模仿策略能完成复杂操作，但执行中的小误差会累积并导致失败；已有精修方法通常需要额外的在线策略学习或代价高昂的在线规划，因此需要一种廉价可优化的精修方式。作者的关键洞察是：预训练策略已提供可用的名义行为，精修只需预测小动作修正如何改变结果。
AI.method: 输入是交互历史与策略给出的动作提议（policy proposal）。方法离线地从"动作扰动后的策略 rollout"中学习局部动作敏感度，得到动作仿射世界模型（A²WM）：它把任务相关几何预测为一条名义轨迹加上对修正量的线性响应，并直接预测整个规划时域，从而避免递归模型调用造成的中间误差传播。精修阶段在预测任务误差上加二次惩罚、对线性修正施加约束，形成廉价的凸二次规划（QP）。在线精修只做一次模型评估和一次 QP 求解，策略与模型权重都保持冻结；相对既有方法的变化是不做额外在线策略学习、也不做昂贵在线规划。
AI.result: 作者报告：在四个仿真操作任务上，该框架在所评估基线中取得最高成功率；平均每个控制步仅增加 3.8 ms 精修开销，且该开销不含基础策略采样。摘要未给出具体成功率数值、基线名称与任务细节。
AI.conclusion: 该工作把"精修"重构为对局部动作响应的廉价凸优化问题，为在冻结预训练策略之上做低开销的推理时误差纠正提供了一种世界模型式思路，并以仿真操作任务的成功率与毫秒级开销作为证据。证据边界：结果仅来自仿真，摘要未报告真机验证、具体成功率数值、基线构成或消融；开销定义明确排除了基础策略采样。

title: From a Single RGB Image to Robot Execution: Metric Scene Alignment and Contact-Guided Retargeting
summary: Extending humanoid interaction generation to new environments remains limited by the need for prebuilt 3D scene assets. Reconstructing scenes directly from single RGB images offers a way to overcome this limitation, but introduces a key challenge in maintaining geometric consistency throughout motion generation and transfer. Visually plausible human motions may be misaligned with the reconstructed scene, while retargeting can introduce additional support errors due to differences between human and robot embodiments. We present a unified pipeline that transforms a single RGB image into a humanoid motion reference. It reconstructs scene geometry from the input image, generates a human interaction conditioned on the reconstructed scene, and retargets the motion to a humanoid robot. To maintain geometric consistency throughout this process, we incorporate two complementary refinement stages before and after embodiment transfer. Before retargeting, Joint Metric Interaction Refinement (JMIR) refines human motion alignment with the registered metric scene while preserving the generated interaction structure. Following retargeting, Contact Guided Residual Retargeting (CGRR) corrects robot specific support errors to restore the intended support relationships. Together, these stages produce motion references that are consistent with the reconstructed scene and can be followed by multiple pretrained humanoid trackers without scene specific policy fine tuning. Compared with GRAIL, our method reduces refinement time from 480 s to 87 s, yielding a speedup of 5.5 times. The complete pipeline achieves a success rate of 89% in simulation and 70% across 50 physical trials on the Unitree G1, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating executable humanoid motion references from single RGB images.

AI.tldr: 该工作用单张RGB图像重建场景、生成受场景约束的人体交互动作并重定向到人形机器人，通过重定向前后两阶段细化保证几何与支撑一致性。作者报告相比GRAIL细化时间从480 s降至87 s（5.5倍加速），流水线仿真成功率89%，在Unitree G1上50次实物试验成功率70%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：把人形交互动作生成扩展到新环境受限于需要预制3D场景资产。直接从单张RGB图像重建场景可绕过该限制，但带来几何一致性难题——视觉上合理的人体动作可能与重建场景错位，而重定向又会因人机具身差异引入额外的支撑错误。
AI.method: 输入是一张RGB图像。流水线先重建场景几何，再以重建场景为条件生成人体交互动作，最后把动作重定向到人形机器人。为保持全过程几何一致性，加入两个互补细化阶段：重定向前，JMIR（Joint Metric Interaction Refinement）在保留生成交互结构的前提下，把人体动作与配准后的度量场景对齐；重定向后，CGRR（Contact Guided Residual Retargeting）修正机器人特有的支撑误差，恢复原本意图的支撑关系。输出是与重建场景一致的机器人运动参考，摘要称其可被多个预训练人体跟踪器直接跟随，而无需针对场景微调策略。
AI.result: 效率方面，作者称相比GRAIL，本方法把细化时间从480 s降到87 s，即5.5倍加速。效果方面，完整流水线在仿真中成功率为89%，在Unitree G1上50次实物试验中成功率为70%。摘要未给出仿真试验次数、任务/场景类型分布，也未报告成功率对比基线或误差指标。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作指向一条从单张RGB图像直通人形机器人可执行运动参考的路径：把"度量场景对齐"放在具身转换之前、"接触引导残差修正"放在之后，来缓解单图重建场景与动作之间的错位以及人机具身差异带来的支撑误差。证据边界：以上仅为摘要中的作者自述，仿真89%与实物70%缺少任务级细分、基线和统计信息；摘要只给出与GRAIL的时间对比，未在成功率上与GRAIL比较，也未说明"多个预训练跟踪器"具体数量与表现。结果未经独立验证。

title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals
summary: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck. Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time. As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.

AI.tldr: 该文用一个固定的障碍物探针检查 RSSM 世界模型：后验状态 AUC 0.85，想象推演状态 15 步内衰减到 0.71，说明信息损失发生在转移模型而非表征。规划器自身的集成不确定性项对此毫无察觉（AUC 0.52，等同随机），构成规划时未被标记的"想象失败"。
AI.motivation: 基于模型的规划器在想象未来时默认转移模型能忠实传递任务相关信息，但摘要指出这一性质"很少被直接测量"，因此是否存在、何时失效缺乏直接证据。
AI.method: 输入是 CARLA 驾驶模拟器中一个 Recurrent State Space Model 世界模型的状态，配合主动推理（active inference）规划。做法是训练一个监督式障碍物探针，先在后验（观测滤波后）状态上测得其可解码性，再把同一个探针原封不动地套用到想象推演出的先验状态上，逐步骤观察信息是否流失；由于探针不变，衰减只能归因于转移模型。随后再检查规划器自带的基于集成的认知（epistemic）项能否识别这一损失。次要部分在同一世界模型上对 Effective Free Energy 各分量做任务条件加权，并引入运行时权重调制。输出是对想象状态信息保真度的量化诊断，以及一个带任务条件加权的规划配置。
AI.result: 作者报告：同一探针在想象先验状态上出现单调衰减，"AUC 0.85→0.71 over 15 steps"，logit 分离度下降 57%；规划器集成分歧作为障碍物分类器仅达 AUC 0.52（随机水平），未能标记该损失；无特权运行时坐标时避障成功率降到 0%。次要贡献在 CARLA 中报告车道保持 81.2 ± 1.8% 路线完成率与 28/28 避障成功（使用特权坐标）。这些均为作者在单种子案例研究中报告的结果。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型的意义在于：想象推演的可用性不能由后验表征质量或规划器内部不确定性代理来保证，需要独立的探针式测量。证据边界很明确——这是单种子、单一模拟器、单一世界模型架构的案例研究，摘要未报告真实机器人验证、多种子统计或跨环境泛化。
AI.core_method: 把同一个冻结的障碍物探针分别作用于后验状态和想象推演状态，用二者的解码差距隔离出转移模型这一信息瓶颈。

key_results.setting: CARLA 驾驶模拟器中单个 Recurrent State Space Model 世界模型 + 主动推理规划；单种子案例研究；探针在两种情况中完全相同（摘要未报告数据集规模、训练细节与统计显著性）。

key_results.finding: 规划器自身的集成式认知项无法察觉上述信息损失：集成分歧作为障碍物分类器仅有 AUC 0.52，即随机水平，作者称其为未标记的想象失败（unknown unknown）。
key_results.setting: 同一世界模型与主动推理规划器；集成分歧被直接当作障碍物分类器评估；摘要未报告集成规模或阈值设定。
key_results.evidence_quote: the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level)

limitations: 作者自述该方法为单种子案例研究（single-seed case study），因此所报告的衰减曲线与 AUC 数值的稳定性、可复现性在摘要中未获支持。
作者报告无特权运行时坐标时避障降到 0%，且次要贡献的 28/28 避障是在使用特权坐标的条件下取得；摘要未说明这一依赖在完整系统中的可替代性。

title: CrowdMAPS: Crowdsourcing Multiple Actions per State for Real-World Imitation Learning
summary: Real-world robot imitation learning is often limited by the cost of collecting physical demonstrations, which typically yield only one action label per visited state. We present CrowdMAPS, a web-based crowdsourcing paradigm for augmenting real-robot datasets with Multiple Actions per State (MAPS). After or during standard robot data collection, CrowdMAPS distributes visited robot states to remote annotators through a web-based 3D interface, where they specify alternative valid actions without requiring access to physical robot hardware. This expands robot datasets along a complementary "width" dimension--by increasing the number of actions per visited state--rather than only by collecting more trajectories. We evaluate CrowdMAPS using keyframe-centric goal-pose annotations supplied by non-expert annotators and train imitation policies on the resulting MAPS data. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, increasing MAPS width from one to ten actions per state improves sample efficiency and increases average success rates by 35.6 percentage points for keypose policies and 33.0 percentage points for trajectory policies. These results show that software-mediated human annotations can augment physical robot data to afford denser supervision, establishing CrowdMAPS as a scalable digital layer for real-robot data collection.

AI.tldr: 真实机器人模仿学习受限于物理演示采集成本高、每个访问状态通常只有一个动作标签。CrowdMAPS 通过网页 3D 界面让远程非专家标注者为已有机器人状态补充其他有效动作，从而在"宽度"维度扩充数据集；作者报告在五个真实操作任务上把每状态动作数从 1 提升到 10，平均成功率提高 35.6（keypose 策略）和 33.0（trajectory 策略）个百分点。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，真实世界机器人模仿学习常受物理演示采集成本限制，而标准采集通常只为每个访问过的状态产生一个动作标签，监督密度不足。作者的动机是在不增加物理机器人采集次数的前提下补充每个状态的替代有效动作。
AI.method: 输入是标准机器人数据采集中（或采集后）访问到的机器人状态。CrowdMAPS 把这些状态通过基于网页的 3D 界面分发给远程标注者，标注者无需接触物理机器人硬件即可指定其他有效动作，从而在同一状态上产生多个动作（Multiple Actions per State, MAPS）。与"只收集更多轨迹"的做法相比，它沿"宽度"维度扩充数据。产出是 MAPS 增强的机器人数据集，随后用于训练模仿策略。摘要中评估采用的是关键帧中心的目标位姿（keyframe-centric goal-pose）标注，标注者为非专家。
AI.result: 作者报告：在五个真实世界操作任务上，将 MAPS 宽度从每状态 1 个动作增加到 10 个动作，可提升样本效率，并使 keypose 策略平均成功率提高 35.6 个百分点、trajectory 策略提高 33.0 个百分点。摘要未给出绝对成功率数值、对比基线细节、任务名称或统计显著性信息。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能数据采集而言，该工作提示：软件介导的人类标注可作为物理机器人数据的补充层，提供更密集的监督，并把数据扩充从"更多轨迹"扩展到"每状态更多动作"。证据边界：以上均为作者自报结果，实验为五个真实操作任务，评估使用非专家的关键帧目标位姿标注；摘要未报告与"多收集轨迹"这一替代方案的可比数值、标注质量/一致性、成本或部署细节，因此"可扩展数字层"仍是作者的主张而非独立验证的结论。
AI.core_method: 把机器人已访问状态通过网页 3D 界面交给远程非专家标注者，为同一状态补写多个有效动作，形成"每状态多动作"的增强数据集来训练模仿策略。
limitations: 作者未在摘要中明确列出局限；摘要自述标注者为非专家，且评估限于关键帧中心的目标位姿标注。

title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
summary: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. However, sampled action sequences can be ineffective, while evaluating alternatives with computationally expensive verifiers adds latency at each policy query. In this work, we propose HDH, a lightweight framework that uses hindsight from a frozen VLA's own deployments to improve action verification. The framework has three stages. First, we deploy the policy and collect its autonomous rollouts. We then train a compact action verifier to assign each action chunk a predicted task-success score. Finally, the frozen VLA generates action candidates, and the verifier selects the candidate with the highest score for execution. Across four LIBERO-10 tasks, HDH achieves an average success rate of 82.3\% and on three real-world manipulation tasks, HDH improves average success over the baseline policy by 22.6\%.

AI.motivation: 摘要指出：VLA模型在通用机器人操作上进展显著，但采样得到的动作序列可能无效；而用计算昂贵的验证器评估替代动作会在每次策略查询时增加延迟。因此需要一个既提升动作有效性、又不引入高验证开销的方案。

title: ILA: A Transferable Interface-Level Adapter for Compliant Humanoid Motion Tracking
summary: Humanoid motion tracking is fundamental to reproducing human motions on humanoid robots and serves as an important tool for teleoperation and motion data collection. However, directly tracking reference motions can be unsafe in constrained environments or during physical human--robot interaction, motivating the need for compliant motion tracking. We present ILA, an Interface-Level Adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. ILA adapts motion references from the robot's observation history, allowing the robot to respond to physical guidance while preserving the capabilities of a pretrained motion tracker. As an interface-level module, ILA can be directly plugged into different pretrained motion trackers without retraining either the adapter or the tracking policies. ILA is trained entirely in simulation to predict reference corrections induced by physical interaction. We evaluate ILA with three humanoid motion trackers and achieve a 63.6--75.4% reduction in guidance-target error compared with their original policies. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance. These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation
summary: We present DroneDiffusion, a perception-aware diffusion planner for local 3-D UAV trajectory generation that explicitly models and avoids failure zones caused by lens flare, overexposure, and reflective surfaces. A vision-language perceptual safety estimator produces a pixel-aligned reliability map that highlights regions of degraded sensing. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is conditioned on this map together with the onboard RGB image, goal point, and initial velocity to generate egocentric 3-D trajectories. To enforce obstacle avoidance at inference time without retraining, we apply training-free CHOMP guidance over a 3-D Euclidean signed distance field. The model is trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot on a real drone. Reliability conditioning raises the mean perceptual reliability along generated trajectories to 0.71, compared with 0.63 for a geometric baseline, while guidance halves the collision rate of the learned prior from 14.7% to 7.8%. Perceptual safety conditioning and geometric guidance are therefore complementary: treating sensor reliability as a first-class signal reduces incursions into unreliable regions while maintaining competitive navigation performance.

AI.tldr: DroneDiffusion 用视觉-语言感知安全估计器生成像素对齐的可靠性图，条件化 DDPM 生成局部 3-D 无人机轨迹，并在推理时用免训练的 CHOMP 引导避免碰撞。作者报告可靠性条件化把轨迹平均感知可靠性从几何基线的 0.63 提升到 0.71，引导把学习先验的碰撞率从 14.7% 降到 7.8%。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型方向的读者，这篇工作把"感知可靠性"作为扩散规划器的一等条件信号，并展示了训练时用可靠性建模、推理时用优化引导分工的路线，且仿真训练可直接迁移到真机。但摘要只给出感知可靠性与碰撞率的两个聚合数字，未说明碰撞率与可靠性具体在仿真还是真机、何种场景下测得，也未给出算力、延迟、成功率和统计显著性，因此证据边界仅限于作者自报的这两项指标。

title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
comment: 35 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables (incl. appendix with supplementary figures and tables). Submitted to The International Journal of Robotics Research. Project page: this https URL . Code: this https URL
summary: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

title: PolyMorphWBC: Whole-Body Control from End-Effector Trajectories for Quadrupedal Mobile Manipulation across Arm Morphologies with Extended Reach
summary: Quadrupedal mobile manipulators can extend their manipulation workspace by coordinating the mounted arm with the mobile base. At the task level, short-horizon end-effector (EE) trajectories provide an interface for specifying the desired manipulation motion without prescribing how it should be realized by the arm and base. However, executing such trajectories remains challenging because the controller must determine when and how the base should move, and this decision depends on the mounted-arm morphology. We therefore present PolyMorphWBC, a hierarchical controller that takes an EE trajectory as the sole task-level motion command and generates coordinated arm--base motions across four families of 6-DoF mounted arms, with extended-reach trajectories beyond the initial fixed-base reach. Within PolyMorphWBC, a trajectory-conditioned coordinator determines the base motion from previewed EE targets, while arm-specific Inverse Kinematics (IK) tracks the current target, and a frozen locomotion backend executes the resulting motion. Cross-arm reuse is enabled by a Unified Robot Description Format (URDF)-derived morphology conditioning, together with online residual-wrench feedback. We train PolyMorphWBC on procedurally generated arms and structured trajectories within and beyond fixed-base reach. In IsaacLab, it achieves 93.95% completion with 2.30cm position error and 4.81° orientation error on held-out trajectories and arm morphologies. In MuJoCo evaluation against UMI-on-Legs, PolyMorphWBC reduces EE position error by 69--72% and orientation error by 91--97% across four within- and extended-reach trajectories. On a physical Go2--ARX5 system, we demonstrate language-conditioned extended-reach pick-and-place using EE trajectories from pi_0 without vision-language-action (VLA)-generated base commands.

title: Low-Cost Mobile Bimanual Manipulation for Long-Horizon Toilet Cleaning
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising capabilities for robot manipulation, but their performance on accessible mobile bimanual platforms remains underexplored. We present a low-cost and reproducible mobile bimanual platform integrating two LeRobot SO-101 manipulators with a TurtleBot 4 and a LeRobot-ROS 2 software stack. Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, we collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate $\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, and GR00T under the same embodiment and task conditions. We further evaluate variants using SARM-derived task-progress signals and short-term MEM observation history. Among the evaluated models, $\pi_0$ performs best, achieving 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, increasing to 90% with limited human intervention. In contrast, the evaluated progress- and memory-augmented variants do not improve their corresponding baselines. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of long-horizon mobile bimanual manipulation on accessible hardware while highlighting remaining challenges in reliable VLA deployment. title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
summary: Bimanual robotic manipulation is versatile, yet its central challenge lies not only in executing dexterous motion with each hand, but also in coordinating the two arms for long-horizon manipulation under coupled spatial and temporal constraints. Prior work has largely focused on endowing robots with human-level manipulation skills, paying less attention to the structure of bimanual behaviour itself: many practical tasks are a coordinated composition of reusable unimanual skills and a small set of synchronous bimanual skills. This makes high-level spatio-temporal coordination, rather than skill acquisition alone, a key bottleneck for efficient bimanual execution. We propose BiPOP, a framework that couples Large Language Models (LLMs) with Temporal Partial-Order Planning for long-horizon bimanual manipulation. At its core is an explicit spatio-temporal model that partitions the workspace by arm reachability and captures inter-arm dependencies, arm assignment, synchronization requirements, and opportunities for safe concurrent execution. Building on this model, an LLM translates natural-language instructions into a formal PDDL specification, while a temporal planner enforces the constraints and schedules actions, yielding plans that are logically consistent at the symbolic level and efficient through parallel execution. On simulated long-horizon tasks of varying complexity, BiPOP outperforms open-loop planning with strong reasoning models and closed-loop ReAct-style planning in success rate, planning time, and plan efficiency, and the full pipeline runs end to end on the real bimanual robot NICOL. A failure analysis further shows that LLM-only planners mainly violate spatial and temporal coordination constraints, which motivates delegating these constraints to a symbolic planner. title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
summary: Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the basic units of both environmental understanding and computation. EMS-Nav groups objects and their relationships into functionally meaningful spaces and builds a hierarchy from local areas to the broader environment. This organization supports efficient map construction alongside the interpretation and execution of language goals at different scales. In multi-scale navigation experiments, EMS-Nav achieves the highest success rates across all four target categories: objects, rooms, regions, and specific instances. It outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping and navigation methods, improving overall first-attempt success by 9.39 percentage points over the strongest baseline while reducing mapping overhead and language-model input size. Local deployment in real indoor environments further demonstrates its applicability to on-device embodied navigation. By establishing regions as the organizing basis for perception, spatial understanding, and language-guided action, EMS-Nav provides a system that combines multi-scale understanding with computational efficiency to support diverse language goals on resource-constrained robots.

title: GraSLA: A Lightweight Spatial-Language-Action Model with Grasp Hypotheses as Geometric Priors
summary: This paper focuses on improving the behavioral diversity and effectiveness of language-conditioned manipulation policies trained through imitation learning. Recently, continuous-action policies have become mainstream in robotic manipulation, but the lack of diverse demonstrations tends to restrict their behavioral diversity. For grasping, a fundamental subtask of manipulation, 6-DoF grasp detection provides diverse grasp hypotheses, but open-loop execution constrains responsiveness in dynamic environments. This motivates us to combine the diversity of grasp hypotheses with the adaptability of continuous-action policies. To this end, we propose GraSLA, a lightweight and effective spatial-language-action model with grasp hypotheses as geometric priors. In particular, we employ spatial and language foundation models to encode scene geometry and task semantics, and integrate them with grasp hypotheses through bidirectional cross-attention for continuous action prediction. On LIBERO, GraSLA achieves an average success rate of 99.30%.

AI.motivation: 摘要指出两个具体缺口：连续动作策略已成为机器人操作主流，但演示数据缺乏多样性，限制了策略的行为多样性；抓取检测（6-DoF grasp detection）虽能提供多样抓取假设，其开环执行又限制了动态环境中的响应能力。作者因此想把抓取假设的多样性与连续动作策略的自适应性结合起来。
AI.method: 输入为场景几何、任务语义与抓取假设三类信息。方法用空间基础模型编码场景几何、用语言基础模型编码任务语义，再通过双向交叉注意力（bidirectional cross-attention）把抓取假设与这两类表征互相整合，最终输出连续动作预测。相对摘要所述的基线（纯连续动作策略、以及开环执行的抓取检测），改变在于把抓取假设从被开环执行的最终动作，改为参与连续动作生成的几何先验。摘要未给出网络结构细节、参数规模或训练设置。

title: Embedded Sim-to-Real Visual Servoing: Learned Reaching and Force-Guided Placement
summary: Embedded perception-to-control systems must combine visual targeting with reliable contact handling under tight computational constraints. We present a shared architecture on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin controlling a Franka Research 3 through Cartesian impedance control. RealSense D435i observations, YOLO11-seg segmentation, depth back-projection, and hand--eye calibration provide metric robot-frame targets. We compare two strategies: compact proximal policy optimization (PPO) policies transferred from simulation for object- and hole-region reaching, and force-guided Cartesian placement using approximately 2 N normal contact and spiral search. The PPO policies achieved 87.2% and 83.1% success over 1000 simulation episodes each. Across 50 real-robot trials per strategy, the learned hybrid and force-guided analytical pipelines achieved 70.0% and 74.0% completion, respectively. Mean perception latency with TensorRT was 34.55 ms. These results support an embedded architecture combining learned free-space reaching with explicit contact correction.

title: Recover, Don't Just Continue: Learning from Feedback for Physical Failure Understanding and Correction
summary: Multimodal large language models are regarded as the cognitive foundation of embodied intelligence, but planning from instructions alone cannot make them reliable. During execution, actions deviate from intended effects, constrained by the embodiment and environment. An embodied brain must understand why execution deviates, identify what can be reliably realized, and revise decisions using interaction experience. These correspond to causal failure localization, capability-constrained adaptation, and experience-driven revision. Current embodied foundation models largely lack these capabilities. To address this, we introduce Embodied-Corrector. We construct failure-recovery data by injecting perturbations at subtask boundaries of successful trajectories, replaying affected subtasks, and keeping failures that are observable from public evidence and recoverable from the current state. We align actions, consequences, failure causes, and recoveries into Judge-Cause-Sub-Fine supervision. Training uses evaluation-first SFT: the model learns Judge and Cause first, then Sub and Fine conditioned on accurate prefixes. Since deployment uses self-generated prefixes, evaluation errors propagate into recovery planning, and response-level rewards are too coarse to locate affected planning tokens. We therefore use OPD to internalize the planning distribution under accurate prefixes into that under self-generated ones: the model generates plans from self-generated prefixes, while a contrastive forward pass with accurate prefixes compares token probabilities to reinforce or suppress planning tokens. At deployment, this branch is removed. Experiments show stronger failure analysis and corrective planning: with a frozen VLA, composite task success improves by 6.1 percentage points; with fixed GPT-5.5 execution, manipulation and navigation tasks improve by 13.9 percentage points.

AI.tldr: 针对多模态大模型仅凭指令规划、执行时动作偏离意图且缺乏失败定位与修订能力的问题，作者提出 Embodied-Corrector：用子任务边界注入扰动构造失败—恢复数据，以 Judge-Cause-Sub-Fine 监督做"先评估后生成"的 SFT，再用 OPD 把"准确前缀下的规划分布"蒸馏到"自生成前缀"上，部署时移除该分支。摘要报告：冻结 VLA 时复合任务成功率提升 6.1 个百分点；固定 GPT-5.5 执行时操作与导航任务提升 13.9 个百分点。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，多模态大语言模型被视为具身智能的认知基础，但"仅从指令规划"无法保证可靠：执行过程中动作会因具身形态与环境约束而偏离预期效果。具身大脑需要理解偏离原因、识别哪些目标可被可靠实现、并利用交互经验修订决策，对应因果失败定位、能力受限适应与经验驱动修订三种能力。摘要称当前具身基础模型大体缺乏这些能力。
AI.method: 输入是成功轨迹与执行中的失败情形。数据侧：在成功轨迹的子任务边界注入扰动、重放受影响的子任务，只保留"可由公开证据观察到且能从当前状态恢复"的失败；并把动作、后果、失败原因与恢复对齐成 Judge-Cause-Sub-Fine 监督。训练分两步：先做 evaluation-first SFT，让模型先学 Judge 与 Cause，再在准确前缀条件下学 Sub 与 Fine；由于部署时用的是自生成前缀、评估误差会传导到恢复规划，且响应级奖励太粗、无法定位受影响的规划 token，作者用 OPD 将准确前缀下的规划分布内化到自生成前缀下——模型从自生成前缀生成计划，同时用准确前缀做对比前向、比较 token 概率以强化或抑制规划 token。输出是具备失败分析与纠正性规划能力的策略；部署时该对比分支被移除。
AI.result: 摘要给出两项改进，均以"百分点"报告而非相对百分比：在冻结 VLA 的设定下，复合任务成功率提升 6.1 个百分点；在执行由固定 GPT-5.5 完成的设定下，操作与导航任务提升 13.9 个百分点。摘要同时概括称实验显示"更强的失败分析与纠正性规划"，但未给出具体基准名称、成功率绝对值、对比基线、数据规模或是否包含真机实验。是否仿真或真机、样本量与显著性均未报告。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与规划研究而言，该工作把"执行偏离"当作一等监督信号：先定位失败原因、再在能力约束下重规划，并用准确前缀与自生成前缀之间的 token 级对比来缓解评估误差向恢复规划的传播，这是对"仅继续执行"式规划范式的一次针对性修正。证据边界明确：摘要只报告两个百分点提升，且未说明实验平台（仿真或真机）、基线定义与统计细节，因此可支持的结论仅限于"作者称失败分析与纠正性规划得到改善"，其泛化性与可靠性未经摘要层面的独立验证。

title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. This raises a critical question: when should a robot policy imagine the future? In this paper, we propose Bind-WAM, a binding-uncertainty-guided WAM for selective future imagination. Bind-WAM introduces language-object binding uncertainty, selectively invoking joint future-action generation when the current observation does not support stable task-relevant action generation. An offline labeling pipeline uses complete demonstrations and action context to identify task-relevant objects and detect reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity drift. The resulting pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight router that predicts binding uncertainty from the current observation and language instruction. At inference, a shared WAM policy invokes selective future imagination according to the predicted uncertainty and its change between consecutive replanning steps. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that Bind-WAM can establish binding uncertainty as a strong, interpretable signal for selective future imagination.

title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. We vary the prediction and execution horizons, compare synchronous and asynchronous inference, test methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapt the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. Short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and methods that keep the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency. title: MOSAIC: Modular Obstacle and Spatial-Aware Framework for Manipulation In Cluttered Scenes
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in robotic manipulation, yet most rely primarily on 2D visual observations and language instructions, leaving scene geometry and obstacle relationships to be inferred implicitly. This limitation is particularly problematic in cluttered environments, where small spatial errors can lead to unintended contacts or collisions. We propose MOSAIC, a modular spatial- and obstacle-aware framework that can be integrated with pretrained VLA policies to improve object-level scene understanding and action generation. Our method augments the VLA backbone with an auxiliary semantic grounding task that predicts role-specific masks for the target object, destination region, and surrounding obstacles. We further combine the target and destination masks with depth estimated from 3D scene reconstruction to construct role-specific geometric tokens that are injected directly into the action expert. In addition, we propose obstacle-aware attention supervision that emphasizes obstacles near the robot body during task execution. The resulting attention features are subsequently injected into later action-expert layers to further guide action generation. Together, these components provide explicit semantic, geometric, and obstacle-aware cues while preserving the underlying pretrained VLA architecture. We evaluate our framework on pretrained VLA model using the RoboPRO benchmark, including visual perturbation tests, and further validate it on real-world manipulation tasks. MOSAIC improves the success rate by 5.1% in cluttered scenes, and by 9.7% under visual perturbations, with gains of up to 25.0% in the most challenging environment. title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO), 2026. Project website: this https URL
summary: Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics. We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage. title: Memory-Efficient Parallel Policy Learning for Collapse-Reactive Retreat via Hybrid Terrain Modeling
summary: At disaster sites and on unstable slopes, robot contact can collapse uninspected terrain, requiring retreat upon support loss. Massively parallel reinforcement learning of collapse-reactive retreat requires independent state--action experiences. However, on shared rigid-body collapsible terrain, one robot's collapse alters others' contacts without direct interaction. We call this indirect interference. Duplicating terrain objects prevents this but is memory-intensive, limiting parallel sampling. Our key insight is that policy learning does not necessarily require rigid-body collapse modeling, which is feasible but computationally expensive; collapse-induced contact responses can suffice. We therefore propose a memory-efficient parallel policy-learning framework for collapse-reactive retreat via hybrid terrain modeling. Hybrid terrain modeling combines rigid-body simulation of non-collapsible terrain with virtual contact forces for collapsible regions. A State-Multiplexed Contact Model shares terrain geometry and a contact-response law while maintaining environment-specific collapse states, enabling independent experiences without terrain objects for collapsible regions. The framework trains a proprioceptive policy for both normal locomotion and collapse-reactive retreat. title: MotionSkill: From Bipedal Motion Video to Control across Embodiments
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Fortune AI technical report
summary: Reusing a demonstrated gait can reduce the work of specifying the same motion for each biped. A video captures the timing of a step, but each robot must execute it with its own limbs and actuators. MotionSkill recovers a timed reference once from monocular video and adapts it to each target in simulation. It aligns root motion and body landmarks in a common frame and records which landmarks are available at each instant. At each source timestamp, the mapper preserves limb directions, uses the target segment lengths, and solves inverse kinematics under joint limits and closure constraints. In MuJoCo, we train a separate residual policy for each of ten bipeds on its mapped reference from one four-second walking clip. Each policy uses the measured robot state to correct joint commands during contact. From initial states held out during training, MotionSkill completed 98% of trials on the original video and 26% with the upper body occluded for one second.

title: Video-Action Models for Data-Efficient Industrial Manipulation
summary: Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation. Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data. We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories. We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform. On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

title: Robot Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance from Randomly Positioned External Cameras
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, accepted as a regular paper for the 2027 IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration
summary: We study robot navigation in indoor environments from fixed exocentric cameras (infrastructure-mounted, external to the robot). We show that standard Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which succeeds with onboard cameras, fails to learn this navigation end-to-end in our setup. This failure results from the perspective mismatch between exocentric observations and egocentric action and goal formulations, which is too complex to resolve from the reward signal alone. To address this, we propose Viewpoint-Invariant Navigation from Exocentric Cameras (VINE). VINE uses an obstacle map estimation network, trained with supervised learning, that takes exocentric images, camera pose, robot pose, and room dimensions as input and produces a viewpoint-invariant obstacle map. This map can be used either by a PPO policy or by a planner such as A*. VINE's map estimation performs better than perspective mapping approaches, handles cameras placed across a wide range of positions and orientations without view-specific tuning, requires only approximate camera pose estimates (noise with a standard deviation of 30cm per axis in x, y, and z and about 20° of rotation error on average), is robust to intrinsic variation, and extends to two-camera setups with partial coverage. Despite operating from cameras randomized in position during evaluation, VINE surpasses the navigation success rate of PPO with an onboard camera in simulated environments.

title: Visibility-Aware Task and Motion Planning with Task-Centric Perception
summary: Long-horizon manipulation under uncertainty remains a challenging problem in robotics. We present \ourmethod{}, an algorithm for Visibility-Aware Task and Motion Planning. \ourmethod{} extends existing deterministic task and motion planning solvers to partially observable object rearrangement tasks, while still being able to take advantage of the efficiency and compositional generalization over long horizons of the base solver. This extension interleaves sensing actions into a plan skeleton that assumed full observability, and uses a novel persistent object-based memory to fuse observations into object mesh hypotheses and an observed occupancy map. We evaluate \ourmethod{} on real-world tabletop rearrangement tasks which feature heavy occlusion and partial visibility and demonstrate that it outperforms baselines that do not perform active perception or have persistent memory.

title: Remember What Changes the Odds: Critic-Gated Event Memory for Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: In long-horizon manipulation, a robot may need to take different actions under identical observations, depending on task progress and the outcomes of earlier attempts. We refer to this ambiguity as decision aliasing. Resolving it requires the policy to maintain memory of its execution history. To reduce the cost of processing full observation histories, recent methods build compact event memories using perceptual, semantic, or kinematic cues. However, these criteria may miss events that matter for task success. We instead propose an outcome-grounded principle: remember events that substantially change the predicted probability of eventual success. Following this principle, we introduce CGEM, a critic-gated event memory that uses a critic to select events with large estimated changes in success probability. Positive and negative changes are encoded as progress and failure records, respectively. Failure records are discarded once the corresponding subtask is completed. In a ten-subtask diagnostic environment with exactly computed success probabilities, CGEM achieves 88.0% success, compared with 0.0% for both a 36-step observation window and a kinematic event memory. Removing failure records reduces success to 1.7%.

title: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU
comment: 18 pages, 5 figures. Code: this https URL
summary: Whole-body motion tracking lets a humanoid robot follow reference motions, but training a tracking policy for a library of motions has usually taken hours of GPU time. SuperMimic showed that the policy can instead be trained by backpropagating through a world model learned from parallel simulation, and InstantTrack added Muon updates, a residual policy around the reference and an averaged deployed policy. We build on both and present BlinkMimic, a recipe that makes this training faster. On a simulated Unitree G1, BlinkMimic trains one policy for all 40 LAFAN1 clips in 3.4 minutes on a single RTX 4090, measured until three consecutive checkpoints reach a normalized return of at least 0.82 with no failed clip (mean of three seeds). We split training time into the cost of an iteration, the iterations needed to fit the motions, and the iterations needed to remove the last failures, and assign each component, inherited or new, to one of these terms. The new components are a step size that decreases once training has progressed, resets directed by failures of the deployed policy under deployment conditions, and GPU graph capture of the whole iteration. A leave-one-out ablation with three seeds per component shows which term each component affects, and further measurements of the gradient, the update rule and the failure cases explain these effects. title: ManiLadder: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Through a Categorized and Multi-Difficulty Level Task Ladder
summary: Recent advances in robotic manipulation have enabled increasingly complex and dexterous behaviors, yet existing benchmarks still focus on simple pick-and-place tasks and lack a systematic framework for measuring progress in robot learning along the axis of task difficulty. We present ManiLadder, a large-scale and organized simulation benchmark for robotic manipulation. ManiLadder contains 112 carefully designed tasks stratified into 4 difficulty levels, with 8 categories in each level, spanning rigid-body and deformable-object manipulation, single-arm and dual-arm settings, and gripper and dexterous-hand end-effectors. To calibrate difficulty, we fix the data amount the same for every task and use a unified flow- matching imitation learning policy under the same training and evaluation protocols, then use its evaluation success rate as an operational empirical difficulty signal. All tasks are iteratively refined until they fall into target difficulty ranges, which are then verified across different random seeds, policies, and agentic learning systems. We further analyze the task properties, compare different policy performances and training settings, analyze task transfer and data scaling behaviors, and conduct real-world experiments showing that the designed tasks preserve their difficulty ordering beyond simulation. ManiLad- der provides a calibrated ladder for measuring, comparing, and advancing robotic manipulation capabilities. More results are available at this https URL .

title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2027). Project page: this https URL
summary: Vision-based dexterous in-hand manipulation requires knowing not only where an object is, but also how it moves. However, most robotic manipulation systems rely on off-the-shelf visual perception models whose outputs are limited to static object masks, geometry, or 6D poses, leaving downstream controllers to infer object dynamics implicitly from noisy visual observations. We present VOKE, a kinematics-aware perception framework that augments existing object and hand-object pose estimators to recover a complete object kinematic state comprising pose, linear and angular velocity, and linear and angular acceleration. VOKE contains two core perception modules and a downstream application study. First, a Pluggable Kinematics Module (PKM) attaches to the output of a standard pose estimator and predicts the object's linear and angular velocity and acceleration from temporal visual features. Second, a Kinematics-guided Pose Refinement Module (KPRM) converts this motion vector into a second-order, motion-prior reference pose and refines the per-frame pose estimates. We evaluate VOKE on DexYCB and OakInk, where it consistently improves object pose estimation across three different backbones and substantially reduces velocity and acceleration estimation error compared with pose differencing. As a downstream application, we use Kinematics-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (KARL) to compare a kinematics-augmented policy with a pose-history baseline. title: PERA: Plug-in Experts for Robotic Actions in Continual Whole-Body Control
summary: Motion imitation enables humanoid robots to acquire whole-body skills such as walking and dancing. However, fine-tuning an entire policy for a new skill can affect existing behaviors, while training a separate policy for each skill increases training and maintenance costs. We present PERA, a method for learning new skills by reusing existing motion capabilities. PERA freezes a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and trains an additional task expert and its routing score using task rewards or teacher-action supervision. In Unitree G1 simulation, each added task module contains approximately 1.03% of the parameters of the base actor. Built on our pretrained policy, PERA successfully completes all ten new tasks. Disabling the expert restores the original computation path of the base policy, which still fully executes all 126 original motions. Enabling the expert also improves the execution of some dance motions not used to train that expert, indicating that its benefits extend beyond its training motions. Experiments with HoloMotion further demonstrate the applicability of PERA to different base policies.

title: STVLA: Spatial-aware and Temporal-memory forVision-Language-Action Models
summary: Robotic manipulation often requires both spatial scene understanding and task history. However, many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely primarily on current observations, without explicitly integrating spatial structure and task history. Appearance-based memories can be sensitive to occlusion and viewpoint changes, while spatial representations of the current scene alone do not preserve how the scene has changed during task execution. We introduce STVLA, a framework that incorporates features from a pretrained visual geometry foundation model into temporal memory alongside visual representations. This allows the policy to recall past scene structure as context for current action decisions. To select informative history, STVLA uses a mathematically grounded scoring rule that balances relevance to the current observation with complementary evidence from memory. Across evaluations on LIBERO, LIBERO-Mem, MIKASA-Robo, and SimplerEnv Bridge, STVLA achieves the highest average success rate among the compared methods on each benchmark. On real-world block stacking, object organization, and phone packaging, it improves success over $\pi_{0.5}$ by $58.33$, $30.00$, and $35.00$ percentage points, respectively. These results support integrating scene geometry into temporal memory to improve manipulation requiring both spatial precision and task history. title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient
summary: Vision-based high-speed navigation requires a trajectory planner that can reactively generate smooth, collision-free trajectories from onboard visual observations. Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to vision-based trajectory planning, as it enables the optimization of sequential decision-making policies in complex environments. However, model-free policy gradient methods rely on sample-based policy gradient estimation, which yields noisy gradient estimates and inefficient training. To this end, we propose a framework for learning trajectory planning policies using the analytic policy gradient (APG) method and use it to train APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner. The proposed framework leverages differential flatness to analytically reconstruct vehicle states from planned trajectories, thereby enabling differentiable trajectory-level state transitions without requiring an explicit low-level dynamics model. By iteratively performing trajectory planning and differentiable state transitions, we construct a differentiable episode rollout and analytically compute policy gradients from episode-level losses, improving both training efficiency and policy performance. After approximately 30 minutes of training on a single GPU, APG-Planner demonstrates comparable or superior performance to existing baseline methods in simulation and achieves speeds of up to 11\,m/s in real-world flight experiments. We further validate the proposed framework on a skid-steer ground robot, demonstrating its applicability to differentially flat robotic systems beyond quadrotors.

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a powerful foundation for robotic scene understanding, task planning, and language-conditioned control. A natural question follows: can these models also decode what a human operator intends while teleoperating a robot, without any explicit instruction? We formulate this as hierarchical intent prediction, jointly inferring the ongoing atomic action and the broader mission it serves from a short visual teleoperation history. To study this, we introduce VI AMO (Vision Intention Action and Mission Ongoing), a dataset of 6,600 episodes from eleven robot sources with 13,653 temporally aligned action annotations and 9,702 mission annotations. Large proprietary models struggle with this problem: on held-out episodes, GPT-4o reaches Sentence-BERT similarities of only 0.563 and 0.470 for action and mission, and GPT-5.6 Luna achieves only 0.581 and 0.554. Fine-tuning a VLM on VI AMO yields our Vision-Intention Model (VIM), which raises these scores to 0.825 and 0.821 and still reaches 0.726 and 0.717 on the 35.4% of test actions with both labels absent from training. Finally, as a downstream application, VIM's predicted mission enables a vision-language-action (VLA) policy to take over from the operator mid-task in a real-world environment unseen during VIM fine-tuning, reducing human teleoperation time by 34.6% relative to GPT-4o and 39.8% relative to GPT-5.6 Luna, while cutting intent-prediction latency by roughly 70% on average.

AI.tldr: 论文把“从短视觉遥操作历史推断操作者意图”形式化为分层意图预测（同时推断当前原子动作与更高层任务使命），发布 VIAMO 数据集并微调 VLM 得到 VIM；在留出片段上把 Sentence-BERT 相似度从 GPT-4o 的 0.563/0.470 提升到 0.825/0.821，并在真实环境下游接管中相对 GPT-4o 减少 34.6% 遥操作时间。
AI.motivation: 视觉语言模型已用于机器人场景理解、任务规划与语言条件控制，但摘要指出一个尚未回答的问题：这些模型能否在没有任何显式指令的情况下，仅凭一段简短的视觉遥操作历史解码人类操作者的意图。作者同时在摘要中说明大型专有模型在该问题上表现不佳（GPT-4o 动作/使命相似度仅 0.563/0.470），这构成了研究动机。
AI.method: 输入是一段简短的视觉遥操作历史；监督信号来自 VIAMO 中时间对齐的原子动作标注与任务使命标注。方法上的变化是对一个 VLM 在 VIAMO 上做微调（而非直接使用大型专有模型），得到 Vision-Intention Model（VIM），输出是当前正在进行的原子动作与它所服务的更宏观使命。下游使用时，VIM 预测出的使命被用来让一个视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略在任务中途从操作者手中接管。摘要未说明模型规模、微调方式、提示格式或是否使用额外模态。
AI.result: 作者报告三类结果：（1）大型专有模型在该任务上困难：留出片段上 GPT-4o 的 Sentence-BERT 相似度为 0.563/0.470（动作/使命），GPT-5.6 Luna 为 0.581/0.554；（2）在 VIAMO 上微调得到的 VIM 把分数提升到 0.825/0.821，且在训练中两层标签均缺失的 35.4% 测试动作上仍达 0.726/0.717；（3）下游真实环境接管中，相对 GPT-4o 减少 34.6%、相对 GPT-5.6 Luna 减少 39.8% 的人类遥操作时间，意图预测延迟平均降低约 70%。这些均为作者报告值，未经独立验证；相似度为无单位分值，时间与延迟数字为相对降幅而非百分点。

title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
summary: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments. A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and proprioceptive states, encouraging the shared trunk to model each embodiment's dynamics. Across 13 task-embodiment pairs spanning five tasks and six robot embodiments, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid, cross-embodiment pretraining raises MXT+'s average normalized task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 over training from scratch. The gains are particularly pronounced under out-of-distribution conditions, where average task progress increases from 0.53 to 0.77. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of broader pretraining mixtures, modular interfaces, and embodiment dreaming, with dreaming producing more similar latent geometry across embodiments. AI.motivation: 通用操作策略有望受益于人类、真实机器人与仿真智能体的互补经验，但形态、感知与控制接口的差异使这种混合演示难以被有效利用。
AI.method: 输入是来自多来源（人类、真实机器人、仿真智能体）的异构演示，先按语义对应的观测模态与动作模态重新组织成可共享的数据结构。方法学习的是 MXT+（Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming）：在每种具身内部，每个观测模态配一个专用 tokenizer、每个动作模态配一个专用专家，而 Transformer 主干跨具身共享；训练时额外加入"具身做梦"目标，预测未来视觉与本体感受状态的隐表示，促使共享主干为每种具身建模其动力学。流程为在此混合数据上预训练，再在目标具身演示上微调，最终产出该目标具身上的操作策略。

title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
summary: Navigation agents use a large language model (LLM) planner to call a vision-language-action (VLA) model. Each episode needs the LLM, adding cost and delay. We distill successful agent experience into the VLA instead of distilling the planner. The VLA then navigates alone at test time. Agent sessions are not VLA demonstrations. They include motions driven by planner tools and sub-instructions, along with detours. We present H2E, a task-level experience distillation method that converts these sessions into VLA training data. Every motion becomes a VLA action under the original task instruction, with the resulting poses as targets. H2E masks the loss on steps that move away from the goal. It labels every visited state within 1 m of the goal as a stop. We then update the VLA with low-rank adaptation. The VLA learns to stop at the goal and find goals the base model never reaches. On all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%.

AI.tldr: H2E 把"LLM 规划器调用 VLA"的整段导航会话转成任务级训练数据，用 LoRA 微调 VLA，使其在测试时无需 LLM 规划器即可单独导航。作者报告在全部 3,189 个 REVERIE-CE val-unseen 回合上，8B VLA 成功率由 35.0% 升至 44.9%。
AI.motivation: 现有导航智能体由 LLM 规划器调用 VLA 执行，每个回合都需要 LLM，带来额外成本与延迟。作者指出直接蒸馏规划器并非其选择，而是希望把成功智能体的经验蒸馏进被调用的 VLA，使 VLA 测试时可独立完成导航。
AI.method: 输入是智能体的成功会话记录，作者强调这类会话不是干净的 VLA 演示：其中包含由规划器工具和子指令驱动的动作以及绕路。H2E 做任务级经验蒸馏：把每一段运动都视作在"原始任务指令"下的一个 VLA 动作，并以实际到达的位姿作为目标；对偏离目标方向的步骤在损失上做掩码；把距目标 1 m 以内的每个访问状态标注为"停止"。产出的数据用于以低秩适配（LoRA）更新 VLA，输出是一个测试时无需 LLM 规划器、能停在目标处并找到基座模型原本到不了的目标的 VLA 策略。
AI.result: 作者报告在全部 3,189 个 REVERIE-CE val-unseen 回合上，H2E 将 8B VLA 的成功率从 35.0% 提升到 44.9%（相对自身基座模型，同一评测集全部回合）。此外作者以定性方式声称 VLA 学会了在目标处停止、并找到基座模型从未到达的目标；该定性说法未给出数值指标。运行形态（仿真或真机）、延迟/成本的实际下降幅度、训练数据规模与统计显著性均未在摘要中报告。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作提出一条以任务级数据复用替代逐回合 LLM 规划的路线：把"智能体—规划器—VLA"会话变成 VLA 自身的监督信号，从而在测试时移除规划器调用。证据边界为：摘要只给出 REVERIE-CE val-unseen 上的成功率数字，未报告真实机器人实验、延迟或成本量化，也未说明与除基座模型外其他基线的比较，因此"测试时不再需要 LLM"的收益目前是作者陈述而非被量化验证的效率结论。

key_results.setting: 具身导航任务，评测集为 REVERIE-CE val-unseen 的全部 3,189 个回合；对比对象为同一 8B VLA 基座模型；摘要未报告是仿真还是真机、是否与其他方法对比。

title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
summary: Learning whole-body mobile manipulation requires demonstrations that coordinate bimanual actions with locomotion across extended workspaces. However, existing interfaces trade off direct robot control, perception and action alignment, and natural operator mobility, making such demonstrations difficult to collect. We introduce HALO, a human-aligned data collection system for whole-body mobile manipulation. The system aligns the operator's perception and action space with the robot while preserving direct physical feedback and natural locomotion. Operators guide the robot end-effectors through kinesthetic teaching and move a low-resistance platform without the deployed mobile base while performing bimanual manipulation. This interface enables more natural whole-body demonstrations, but the close human-robot coupling introduces discrepancies between the demonstration and deployment settings. We address these discrepancies with deployment-aligned demonstration processing, which calibrates and temporally aligns platform motion with the deployed base response and masks and inpaints demonstrator hands in recorded observations. Compared with Mobile ALOHA and VR teleoperation, HALO enables up to 2.9x faster demonstration collection while maintaining comparable or higher success rates. Policies trained with HALO perform precise manipulation tasks, including zip-tie fastening, and achieve a 73.3% success rate on a six-stage long-horizon mobile manipulation task involving repeated coordinated base and arm motion. title: Inner Product Regularization for Imitation Learning
summary: Robots that learn from demonstrations should extrapolate their policy despite state perturbations such as sensor noise, scene variation, and compounding errors. One approach to this robustness is regularization. Prior regularizers consider each state on its own and limit how sensitive the policy is to any perturbation at that state. By contrast, we explore how the policy's output shifts when given the same perturbation at different states. Our insight is that, locally, the robot should respond to state perturbations in a consistent manner: e.g., if changing an irrelevant object position does not impact the policy at one state, that same change should not shift the policy output at a nearby state. Applying this insight, we develop inner product regularization (InneR). We show that the inner product on action space induces an inner product on state space through the policy Jacobian (the Fisher information for stochastic policies), and that the null space of this inner product governs which state perturbations have a first-order effect on the policy. By clustering states whose inner products are aligned, averaging the inner products within each cluster, and minimizing the smallest eigenvalues of that average, InneR shapes the learned policy so that nearby states share a common null space. InneR enforces consistent responses to perturbations without limiting policy expressiveness, and can be appended to existing imitation learning pipelines for deterministic or stochastic policies. In simulated experiments, InneR makes learned policies more robust to irrelevant state dimensions and shifts between training and test distributions, whereas norm penalties often perform worse than behavior cloning. On a real robot arm performing three manipulation tasks, InneR raises the average success rate of a diffusion policy from 18% to 57% without additional data.

AI.method: 输入是示范数据训练的策略及其对状态的雅可比。作者指出动作空间内积可通过雅可比诱导状态空间内积（随机策略下为 Fisher 信息），其零空间决定哪些状态扰动对策略有一阶影响。InneR 先聚类内积方向对齐的状态，再平均簇内内积并最小化该平均内积的最小特征值，使邻近状态共享一致的零空间。输出是经正则化塑造的策略，可接入已有模仿学习流程，适用于确定性或随机策略；作者称它不限制策略表达能力。

title: SPIRE: Task-agnostic embodied continual learning through autonomous situation inference and causal motor-primitive reuse
summary: Embodied continual learning requires controllers to infer changing situations, retain prior behavior and reuse motor skills without task labels or known boundaries. The challenge is deciding when to recover earlier behavior and which skills can support new learning. We introduce Situation-guided Primitive Integration for Recurrent Embodiment (SPIRE), a recurrent-spiking system that infers latent contexts from action-outcome evidence and learns context-specific motor actors online. Mature actors become protected sources that combine with a target-context residual to drive recurrent-spiking motor populations. Across coordinate, three-joint and hidden-force control, SPIRE maintained control, autonomously inferred situations, retained prior behavior and accelerated acquisition of an unseen source composition, reducing mean interactions to criterion by approximately 40% relative to matched fresh controllers. Rewinding compatible source actors impaired early acquisition in every matched intervention, demonstrating causal reuse. Against seven recurrent continual-learning and modular-control comparators, SPIRE achieved 2.4 times the mean prior-learning advantage of the strongest eligible task-free alternative selected for each paired stream. These results demonstrate autonomous recovery and causal reuse of motor skills for new learning in continuous embodied control.

title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience
summary: Recent advances in frontier models have pushed the boundaries of agentic robot control, enabling agents to perform complex robotic tasks through reasoning and interaction. However, repeated calls to these models during execution can substantially increase task completion time. Code as Policies (CaP) offers a route for coding agents to acquire physical skills through experience and retain them in executable programs, allowing the reasoning invested in development to be reused across runs. Developing reliable code policies while limiting the cost of physical experimentation remains a central challenge. We investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies. Our findings favor robot demonstrations available on request and simulation used selectively during real-world policy refinement. These findings inform ACE-CaP-0, an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieve 92.1\% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop. These results highlight CaP's potential to turn experience into reliable, reusable physical skills.

AI.motivation: 前沿模型让智能体式机器人控制能做复杂任务，但执行期间反复调用这些模型会显著增加任务完成时间。Code as Policies（CaP）可把开发期投入的推理固化在可执行程序中、跨多次运行复用，因此核心挑战是：如何在限制物理实验成本的前提下，得到可靠的代码策略。

title: Scaling VLA Serving Under Robotic Execution Constraints
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation. In our production setting, hundreds of VLA-powered robots are already operating in real-world environments, creating an immediate need for efficient fleet serving. We present XInfer, a production-deployed VLA serving system designed to reduce the inference infrastructure cost of large-scale robotic deployments. XInfer jointly coordinates heterogeneous VLA computation with the evolving response requirements of robotic execution. By exploiting computational parallelism while managing interference, XInfer improves GPU efficiency while protecting time-critical robotic feedback. We evaluate XInfer across three VLA models using production-derived workloads, achieving 1.26-3.75 times the effective robot capacity (ERC) of state-of-the-art systems under physical-execution constraints. Our implementation is publicly available at this https URL .

title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
summary: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.

title: Genie Sim Benchmark: Real-to-Sim Fidelity and Evaluation
summary: We evaluate Genie Sim Benchmark through paired real-simulation tasks and complementary system-identification studies. Across 22 robot-task pairs spanning 16 task names, task-specific pi0.5 policies fine-tuned on real-robot data achieve a descriptive Score correlation of 0.9686, MAE 0.0405, RMSE 0.0520, with simulation-real differences from -0.110 to +0.080. G2 crsB experiments assess long-horizon closed-loop position and joint-side torque agreement, while five representative object cases examine identification and cross-engine contact transfer. A separate 32.6503 s teleoperation trajectory, excluded from mechanical identification and servo-gain search, evaluates external position targets through simulated motion-controller command shaping and a calibrated position servo. Across both arms, per-joint position RMSE spans 0.00614-0.03522 rad and current-derived torque RMSE spans 0.73545-4.00099 N m. Native PhysX adaptations recover three recorded interaction tasks, with case-dependent alignment gains. These results support task-specific simulation evaluation through joint assessment of task outcomes and physical-response consistency.

title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?
comment: Presented at "Do Robots Need World Models?" Workshop at Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2026
summary: Embodied world models (WMs) are implicit learning systems that predict the next future latent state directly from observations and actions. Unique from other end-to-end learning systems, the dynamics predictor of WMs can simulate the environment's response to alternative actions without physical deployment nor pre-specifying states of the dynamical system. Current metrics focus on the quality of model outputs, e.g., clarity of reconstructions or task success, but fail to assess the fidelity of modeling consequences of counterfactual actions. Inspecting the forced response to action perturbations through sensitivity analysis is one way to audit how well WMs can predict the consequences of counterfactual actions. Deploying WMs on hardware will require new evaluation frameworks to analyze the tradeoffs between state error and accurate sensitivity prediction.

title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
summary: Open-world navigation requires a robot to locate a user-specified target in an indoor scene under open-vocabulary queries. Realistic indoor environments are semi-static: walls and furniture largely persist while smaller objects move, relocate, or vanish between visits. Prior-map systems answer queries from object poses recorded at reconstruction time, which expire as soon as objects move, whereas online methods re-derive where to look from current observations every few steps, often through expensive calls to a vision--language model. Assuming that walls and large furniture do not move, we keep their map to plan paths, but use a target--furniture co-occurrence prior to decide where to search. We present PreNav, an ObjectNav framework on semi-static environments. Rather than invoking a vision-language model at each step, PreNav generates a single global search reference before the robot moves: an LLM converts target--furniture co-occurrence into a spatial prior, a conditional diffusion model turns that prior and the persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it, and the robot approaches the target once it is detected online. Experiments on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark show that PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors, using a generator trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries further validate the approach.

AI.tldr: 面向半静态室内环境中的开放词汇目标导航，PreNav 在机器人出发前一次性生成全局搜索参考：LLM 把目标—家具共现转为空间先验，条件扩散模型结合持久结构生成带缓冲带的有序中心线，机器人仅在在线检测到目标后才前往。作者称其在 Gibson ObjectNav 基准上优于强在线基线，但摘要未报告任何数值。
AI.motivation: 真实室内环境是半静态的：墙和大件家具基本不变，小物体在两次到访之间会移动、换位或消失。基于先验地图的系统用重建时刻记录的物体位姿回答查询，物体一移动这些位姿就失效；在线方法则每隔几步就从当前观测重新推断该去哪里找，往往伴随昂贵的视觉—语言模型调用。摘要指出的缺口是：既要避开过期的物体位姿，又要避免高频的 VLM 调用。
AI.method: 输入包括开放词汇的目标查询、持久结构信息（在“墙与大件家具不移动”的假设下保留其地图用于路径规划）以及目标—家具共现关系。流程分两步：一个 LLM 把目标—家具共现转换成空间先验；一个条件扩散模型接收该空间先验与持久结构，输出一条有序中心线及其外围带状区域，作为单个全局搜索参考。相对所述基线（按重建时刻物体位姿作答的先验地图系统、以及每步重推并调用 VLM 的在线方法），PreNav 把“该去哪里找”的决策提前到移动之前一次性完成，不再逐步调用视觉—语言模型；机器人在线检测到目标后即前往目标。
